headline: The Mini Moot 2026
eligibility: Open to University of Guelph-Humber students only
description: The Mini Moot is our in-house moot court competition, run by the Pre-Law Society exclusively for Guelph-Humber students. It's the friendliest place to argue your first moot — no experience needed, and everyone is coached through it.
about:
The Mini Moot is an internal moot court competition organized by the Guelph-Humber Pre-Law Society and open only to students of the University of Guelph-Humber. It runs on the same format as The GH Cup — written skeleton arguments followed by oral advocacy before a panel of judges — at a scale built for people arguing their first case.

It exists so that Guelph-Humber students can learn the format, get feedback, and build confidence among their own classmates before representing the school at inter-university competitions. Many of the advocates who compete for Guelph-Humber across Ontario started here.
howItWorks: Teams of two compete on behalf of either the appellant or respondent
A case problem is released in advance, with prep sessions run by the Society
Competitors submit written skeleton arguments before the oral rounds
Oral rounds are judged by upper-year students, alumni, and legal professionals
Every competitor gets individual feedback, whatever round they finish in
Awards are given for best oral advocates and best written submissions
